flows.carries: idempotent startup: DB migration -> orphan cleanup -> TTS Server subprocess spawn+READY handshake -> plugin discovery -> task recovery
flows.invariant: boot_studio() is idempotent (global _booted flag); TTS server boot runs in a background thread so the web server isn't blocked; recovery runs only after reconciliation and listener registration so progress events reach the UI
failure_modes: DB migration raises -> boot_studio() propagates (no partial-migrated state left running); startup_event catches at the thread boundary and logs, web server still serves static/API routes but DB-backed endpoints fail until restart

TTS Server subprocess never reaches READY within the watchdog's timeout -> circuit breaker trips, watchdog retries with backoff (app/engines/watchdog.py) rather than blocking the web server indefinitely
recovery finds a task whose on-disk artifacts no longer validate -> treated as not-recoverable (reconciliation is the source of truth, not raw file existence) rather than resurrecting a stale job

flows.carries: chapter render request -> chunked/grouped text -> HTTP call into TTS Server subprocess -> plugin synthesis -> WAV written to chapter dir -> progress/ETA broadcast over WebSocket
flows.invariant: orchestrator never talks to the plugin directly; it always routes through VoiceBridge -> HTTP -> TTS Server subprocess, even for engines that are 'local' (XTTS)
failure_modes: TTS Server subprocess unreachable/down mid-request -> bridge_remote/tts_client HTTP call fails, orchestrator publishes a failed job rather than hanging the request
plugin synthesize() raises inside the subprocess -> surfaced back through the HTTP response as a structured error, never a raw traceback to the caller (app/engines/errors.py)

WebSocket broadcast fails/no listeners connected -> progress is still recorded server-side (DB/state.json) and available via REST snapshot on reconnect; broadcast is best-effort, not the source of truth

flows.carries: one chapter split into groups by character/profile/engine; each group rendered through its own sub-engine via bridge; markers (START_SEGMENT/PROGRESS/SEGMENT_SAVED) drive weighted chapter-level progress across heterogeneous engine speeds; final stitch into one chapter WAV (this is the sequential path, still live at cap=1 or for non-segment-orchestrated callers; see parallel-segment-fanout for the concurrent path once a manifest raises max_concurrent_workers)
flows.invariant: INV-6: the orchestrator/worker_metrics owns performance-sample writing; the mixed handler itself never records calibration metrics to avoid poisoning ETA history
failure_modes: one sub-engine group fails mid-chapter -> the whole chapter render fails rather than silently stitching a partial WAV with a gap (no partial-success chapter output)
a sub-engine's marker stream stalls/never emits SEGMENT_SAVED -> that group's weighted progress share stops advancing but does not fabricate completion; the chapter-level progress reflects the stall
stitch_segments encounters a missing/corrupt group WAV -> raises rather than producing a chapter WAV with silence spliced in

flows.carries: raw engine progress line -> velocity-ring sampling -> confidence-weighted ETA crossfade (calculated->observed) -> WebSocket frame -> frontend reducer with status-regression/progress-regression guards -> animated progress bar with its own client-side lane-migration smoothing
flows.invariant: confidence and ETA are never fabricated; frontend only trusts backend-computed confidence for §4A frames (chapters.progress/jobs.lifecycle) and only falls back to computeProgressConfidence() for older non-enriched frames (segments.progress/voice.test) ; eta_updated_at is deduped by ProgressService.enrich() but must be explicitly re-extracted and threaded through app/api/ws.py#broadcast_job_updated into build_chapter_progress_event -- that function's own default (time.time() when omitted) silently defeats the dedupe at the wire on every tick if the extraction is dropped (escaped defect, fixed 2026-07-06); the chapter-fanout parent's own "running" frame (segment_synthesis.py#_publish_progress) now also computes eta_seconds via decay of the dispatch-time estimate rather than leaving it None (2026-07-07 fix -- see parallel-segment-fanout flow for the decay mechanics) Task 013 (2026-07-11): BracketedEtaTracker (eta.py, W-PAR 007) is now wired into ProgressService.publish() at the SEGMENT_SAVED transition and onto the chapters.progress payload as eta_low_seconds/eta_high_seconds/eta_display -- previously built and unit-tested but never fed real data or exposed on the wire.
failure_modes: a §4A-enriched frame's eta_updated_at is dropped during re-extraction -> the wire-level dedupe in ProgressService.enrich() is silently defeated and the frontend can receive an unnecessarily-refreshed timestamp on every tick (escaped defect, fixed 2026-07-06 — see the invariant field)
engine progress markers arrive out of order or a PROGRESS line is malformed -> parse_engine_progress (app/engines/behavior.py) is expected to skip/ignore rather than crash the watchdog's log listener
frontend receives a status-regression or progress-regression frame (e.g. a stale re-delivered event) -> jobUpdateReducer.ts's regression guards drop it rather than visually rewinding the bar

the chapter-fanout PARENT itself must never flow through _dispatch_segment (would register a spurious idle log_listener); a concurrent child must never call handle_mixed_job directly (would re-trigger chapter-terminal stitch/DB-rebuild once per child instead of once per chapter) and must have skip_registry_dispatch=True (else falls through to the legacy per-engine registry handler and silently re-renders a sibling's remaining work — escaped defect, fixed 2026-07-05); synthetic fan-out children emit segment-scoped frames but no durable job rows (ephemeral TaskContext routes through ProgressService.publish(ephemeral=True), suppressing only jobs.lifecycle/queue.items/chapters.progress); chapter progress is size-weighted (grouped_progress from child text-length sums) and order-independent; an explicit backend active_segments_map={} ('nothing rendering') always wins over the frontend's segmentProgress-derived fallback (useStudioChapter.ts) ; the parent's own _publish_progress(status="running", completed=0, ...) must fire immediately after futures submission (not only inside as_completed) or the parent job's status field sticks on "preparing" for the whole first chunk group (fixed 2026-07-06); a child tick's SEGMENT_PENDING/LOADING_MODEL sub-phase is conveyed via reason_code, not status -- _on_child_segment_tick must check both or the preparing pulse is lost (fixed 2026-07-06); 2026-07-07 fix: the chapter-scope _publish_progress "running" frame now computes and durably persists eta_seconds itself (via _dispatch_eta_seconds decayed by grouped_progress/progress, in _live_chapter_eta_seconds) through update_job(skip_job_updated=True) on every frame -- previously only the dispatch-time snapshot was durable and every later tick re-broadcast that frozen t=0 value for the whole render; eta_seconds is now omitted (not passed as explicit None) when no calibration exists so it does not clobber the ticks' own projection-derived ETA (fable-review fix, same day); a successful child tick now leaves a transient {phase:"done", progress:1.0, eta_seconds:0} marker in active_segments_map instead of popping (keeps the frontend's just-finished segment text lit via ScriptView liveDoneSpanIds / useStudioChapter chapterRenderDoneSegmentIds), while failed/cancelled children still pop -- run()'s as_completed loop now passes the child's real status (not a hardcoded "done") into _on_child_segment_tick so a permanently-failed child is never mismarked done (real bug, fixed in fable review same day) Task 014 (2026-07-11): ResourceClaim.cap is now ALWAYS the manifest structural ceiling (grow-only, never the live/effective value); the live/effective admission limit is resolved fresh on every reserve_task_resources call via cap_settings.resolve_effective_cap and passed as EngineClassSemaphore.try_acquire's `limit` param, so a tts_parallel_cap/tts_engine_caps settings change now reaches already-queued and already-running fan-out children within one retry cycle instead of requiring a process restart.
failure_modes: skip_registry_dispatch missing/False on a fan-out child task -> registry handler re-renders all remaining chapter groups per child, and the first-dispatched child silently does every sibling's work too (fixed 41c9d84c)

flows.carries: a per-child marker protocol (START_SYNTHESIS/START_SEGMENT/PROGRESS/SEGMENT_SAVED, each line task_id-tagged) that crosses an HTTP boundary AND a shared-process-stream boundary -- multiple concurrent requests (ENGINE_CLASS_ADMISSION on) run parse_output on different threadpool threads inside the SAME server process, all relaying to the SAME stderr that the watchdog reads and fans out to every registered per-child listener
flows.invariant: the TTS Server is one long-lived process serving N concurrent /synthesize requests on a thread pool; any plugin-side write to the shared process stdout/stderr MUST go through a single-writer-locked emitter (tts_engines/tts_xtts/plugin/server/engine.py#_emit_stderr_atomic) -- a bare print(file=sys.stderr) issues two unsynchronized write() calls (content, then newline) that can interleave with another thread's writes mid-line; watchdog.py's log_listener filter (orchestrator_helpers.py:825) only rejects a line whose EXTRACTED task_id explicitly mismatches -- a line with no extractable task_id, or a merged line whose first-matched marker's task_id happens to match, is NOT rejected and can poison a listener's sticky active_seg_id state (PROGRESS lines carry no segment id of their own, only pct + task_id) until that task's own next real START_SEGMENT arrives
failure_modes: two concurrent requests' unsynchronized print(file=sys.stderr) calls interleave mid-line -> one merged physical line embeds two distinct markers -> the watchdog's per-marker parsing (sequential ifs, not elif) can accept BOTH embedded markers under DIFFERENT extraction rules, so a correctly-tagged listener's active_seg_id gets poisoned by a foreign sibling's segment id, then every subsequent legitimate same-task PROGRESS tick is misattributed to the wrong segment (escaped defect, fixed 2026-07-06: _emit_stderr_atomic write-side lock + orchestrator_helpers.py foreign-sid guard read-side defense + watchdog.py merged-line tripwire diagnostic)

a WarmWorker's _relay_trailing_stderr grace window (fixed 0.3s) elapses before a slow trailing marker line is drained -> the stale line sits in that worker's _stderr_q -> the NEXT job handed to the SAME reused worker relays the stale, un-task-id'd line under the new job's task_id via relay_marker -- a second, independent cross-attribution channel (fixed 2026-07-06: WarmWorker.run_job discards any stale _stderr_q entries before writing the new job to stdin)

app/tts_server.purpose: Self-contained ASGI subprocess: plugin discovery/loading, settings/verification, health, server-side synthesis dispatch. Must not import app.api/orchestration/db/domain/jobs

app/orchestration.purpose: Task lifecycle (submit/cancel/recover), scheduling/fairness/resource gates, and centralized progress/ETA math

app/domain.purpose: Domain layer: voices/chapters/projects/artifacts/settings/jobs models+services+repositories. Mostly Phase-1 scaffolds (NotImplementedError) except voices/chapters which are live

app/jobs.purpose: LEGACY worker-loop handlers (registry, voice worker, audiobook assembly, bridge_helpers) — partially superseded by app/orchestration but still actively dispatched for voice_build/voice_test/assembly and used by all TTS plugin handlers

app/studio_plugin_sdk.purpose: Public SDK plugins import: context object exposing late-bound app.* service groups, job dataclasses, SDK exceptions
depends_on: app/db, app/api/ws.py, app/engines, app/utils (all late-imported inside methods)

app/core.purpose: Cross-cutting: path/storage config, explicit boot sequence, security (API key/rate-limit)

app/storage.purpose: Central storage manager: trusted-root path resolution and validation for projects/voices/uploads

app/utils.purpose: Path-traversal-safe file helpers, text processing/sanitization/splitting, subprocess helpers, render/socket tracing

tts_engines/tts_xtts.purpose: Local GPU voice-cloning engine plugin (XTTS). Warm-worker subprocess pool for model reuse across renders
notes: Execution topology: the TTS Server is a single long-lived process; uvicorn/Starlette serves concurrent /synthesize requests on its threadpool (run_in_threadpool), so N requests can run this plugin's synthesize()/parse_output concurrently on different threads inside ONE process. Module-level mutable state and shared streams (stdout/stderr) are cross-request shared -- see tts-server-shared-stream-single-writer invariant and the tts-server-marker-relay flow.

tts_engines/tts_voxtral.purpose: Cloud voice engine plugin calling Mistral's Voxtral TTS API

tts_engines/tts_mixed.purpose: Composite engine: orchestrates multiple sub-engines per chapter (multi-group render), delegation-only (no local synthesis)

frontend/src/app.purpose: App shell: routing, layout (TopBar/NavRail/PlayerBar), navigation model/breadcrumbs, providers (stubs)

frontend/src/store.purpose: Client state: socket bus, live job overlays, player bus, audit log, notifications/editor-session stubs

frontend/src/api.purpose: REST client (~60 endpoints), WebSocket contract types (liveEvents.ts), hydration coordinator merging overlays with snapshots

frontend/src/hooks.purpose: Data-fetching and live-state hooks: useJobs/useQueueSync (core), chapter/* composite hooks, voice management, playback

frontend/src/components.purpose: Cross-page shared UI: PredictiveProgressBar (ETA confidence model), queue widgets, forms, overlays, layout primitives

frontend/src/pages/Book.purpose: v3.7 IA: BookLayout + 6 stages (Book/Contents/Cast/Studio/Review/Publish/Lexicon -- 'Book' added 2026-07-09 as the new front door, first in stage order and the default landing tab via lib/stages.ts's getLastStage()) sharing BookDataContext; Studio stage hosts the chapter editing workspace (CastPalette + ScriptView); Book stage hosts the front-door hero (BookInfoCard: identity + inline-editable description + Continue Listening + demoted metadata).

frontend/src/pages/ChapterEditor.purpose: Segment/character/voice editing components reused by both legacy ChapterEditorPage and the Book Studio stage

frontend/src/pages/Voices.purpose: Voice catalog + Voice Lab workspace (samples/build/test/ready phase machine)

frontend/src/demo.purpose: Self-contained scripted demo renderer (scene-script engine + REST/socket shims) built separately, published to docs/demo/ via build:demo — lower priority, not wired into production launch

transforms: app/api/contracts/events.py#build_chapter_progress_event / build_queue_item_status_event — DB/state.json Job dict -> topic-scoped wire payload (snake_case additive fields like active_segments_map, no camelCase variant)

frontend/src/types/index.ts#Job — the wire shape as consumed by the frontend; several fields are 'computed but not wired' placeholders (e.g. chapter_wall_duration) present in state.json/wire but not yet read by any UI
Job.notes: Two representations that must be kept straight: the DURABLE DB row (app/db/models.py, SQLite) vs. the LIVE in-memory job dict in state.json (app/db/state_jobs.py) — the live dict is a superset carrying transient fields (active_segment_id, active_segments_map, timing scalars) the DB row doesn't have. A synthetic fan-out child (_SyntheticSegmentTask, ephemeral=True) never gets its own durable Job row at all (INV-4, W-PAR enable-gate) — only the parent ChapterSynthesisTask does.

transforms: app/db/state.py#update_job(active_segments_map=..., skip_job_updated=True) — written straight to job state, bypassing ProgressService.publish (which doesn't carry this field)

app/api/ws.py#broadcast_job_updated -> app/api/contracts/events.py#build_chapter_progress_event -> wire payload.active_segments_map (delivery leg added 2026-07-05; before this, a populated map could never reach the frontend regardless of backend state)

frontend/src/pages/Book/studio/useStudioChapter.ts — when the backend field is undefined (not an explicit {}), falls back to a locally-derived map built from frontend/src/hooks/useJobs.ts's segmentProgress stream
active_segments_map.notes: Shape: dict[segment_id, {phase: 'preparing'|'rendering'|'done', progress: number, eta_seconds: number|null, reason_code?, indeterminate?}]. An explicit backend {} means 'nothing genuinely rendering right now' and MUST win over the frontend's local fallback — only a missing/undefined field triggers the fallback. Additive-only field (INV-1/INV-9): absent when the dispatch path has nothing concurrent to report, never required.

Settings.defined_in: app/db/state_settings.py#_default_state (settings sub-dict; no dataclass, plain dict)
written_by: app/api/routers/system.py#save_settings (POST /api/settings — JSON body branch and form-encoded branch parse DIFFERENT field subsets; tts_parallel_cap/tts_engine_caps are JSON-only)
transforms: app/api/routers/system.py#_redact_settings — strips secret fields (API keys) before the dict ever reaches a JSON response
frontend/src/types/index.ts#Settings — the wire shape; tts_parallel_cap/tts_engine_caps added 2026-07-06
Settings.notes: Settings-then-env fallback pattern used by BOTH api_priority_mode/TTS_API_PRIORITY and tts_parallel_cap/TTS_PARALLEL_CAP: the env var only matters before state.json has ever been normalized (fresh install) — _normalize_settings always materializes a concrete default afterward, so raising a value on a running install must go through the Settings API/UI, never the env var. GeneralSettingsPanel.tsx's existing updateBooleanSetting/updateStringSetting helpers POST form-encoded bodies and silently can't set tts_parallel_cap — a trap for future settings additions unless they're also added to system.py's form branch or use the JSON POST pattern instead.

transforms: app/api/contracts/events.py#normalize_to_canonical_command / LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL — reason_code strings get normalized to a canonical JobLifecycleCommand before topic-scope checks
app/api/ws.py#ConnectionManager broadcasts the same envelope to every subscribed client verbatim — no per-client reshaping
StudioSocketEnvelope.notes: One envelope type, many topics (chapters.progress, segments.progress, queue.items, jobs.lifecycle, chapters.lifecycle, segments.lifecycle, tts_log, voice.test, system, projects.lifecycle). Payload shape is topic-specific (see e.g. ChapterProgressPayload); frontend contract types in liveEvents.ts are the enforced shape for tests per testing-standards.md R3 (contract-shaped event frames, no untyped hand-rolled frame literals).
